tagline: Global renewable energy developer and independent power producer
hero_kpi_rationale: Exceptional revenue growth (46% YoY in 2025) and rapid installed capacity expansion (+22.8% YoY), supported by commissioning of utility-scale projects in Europe and the U.S., demonstrating successful execution of the business model.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue from electricity sales across all operational renewable energy projects.
kpis.description: Revenue is growing strongly, driven by increasing operational capacity, particularly in the U.S. where PPA prices are rising significantly.
kpis.signal: Strong revenue growth driven by new operational projects and higher electricity prices in the U.S.

kpis.name: Operating Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit generated from operations before taxes and interest expenses.
kpis.description: Operating profit is increasing significantly, supported by revenue growth and improved operating margin.
kpis.signal: Strong operational leverage and improved project returns

kpis.name: Net Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit remaining after all expenses, taxes and interest are paid.
kpis.description: Net profit nearly doubles year-on-year, reflecting rising profitability and efficient management of the capital structure.
kpis.signal: Exceptional profit growth and improved financial performance

kpis.name: Installed Capacity
kpis.explanation: Total electric generation capacity of all operational and under-construction renewable energy projects.
kpis.description: Installed capacity is growing rapidly, driven by completed projects and those in final construction stages in Europe and the U.S.
kpis.signal: Rapid expansion of renewable energy generation platform

kpis.name: Electricity Generation
kpis.explanation: Total amount of electricity produced by all operational renewable energy projects.
kpis.description: Electricity generation is increasing significantly, supported by commissioning of new projects, particularly in Europe and the U.S.
kpis.signal: Strong generation growth aligned with capacity expansion

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €8.63 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €5.12 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Cash & Equivalents
kpis.description: Cash & equivalents extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Cash & equivalents of €0.53 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: PPA Revenue Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of electricity revenue generated through long-term PPAs vs. merchant market sales.
kpis.description: The share of revenue from long-term PPAs increases to 80% in 2025 (vs 75% in 2024), enhancing cash flow stability and predictability.
kpis.signal: Increasing revenue stability through long-term PPA contracts

kpis.name: U.S. Revenue Contribution
kpis.explanation: Percentage of total electricity revenue generated from U.S. operations.
kpis.description: U.S. revenue contribution rises from 2% in 2024 to 26% in 2025, reflecting successful entry into the U.S. market with attractive PPA pricing.
kpis.signal: Significant geographic diversification into U.S. market with higher PPA prices

kpis.name: U.S. Solar PPA Prices
kpis.explanation: Average price received for electricity under long-term PPAs in the U.S. solar market.
kpis.description: U.S. solar PPA prices have increased by 99% since early 2021, driven by rising electricity demand from data centers and ongoing electrification.
kpis.signal: Favorable pricing environment driven by strong electricity demand and data center expansion

risks.title: Uncertainty of financial estimates
risks.summary: The company cannot reconcile its non-IFRS measures (EBITDA) with future net results as many items are beyond its control or cannot be predicted. Revenue and performance projections are subject to significant uncertainties.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned at the beginning of the document with strong language ('materially differ', 'unpredictable impact'). Capital category heavily weighted. Stable but structural trend due to nature of development projects. Directly impacts reliability of EBITDA and cash flow forecasts.

risks.title: Multiple currency exchange rate risk
risks.summary: The company operates in multiple currencies (dollar, euro, Israeli shekel) and consolidates its financials in U.S. dollars. Exchange rate fluctuations can significantly affect consolidated financial results and the value of foreign assets.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified mid-document with explicit exposure to EUR, NIS and USD. Neutral language but data shows volatility (EUR: 1.07-1.17, NIS: 0.27-0.30). Stable but structural trend. Geographically diversified portfolio (U.S., Europe, Israel, MENA) amplifies exposure.

risks.title: Dependence on U.S. tax credits
risks.summary: U.S. projects (73% of portfolio) are highly dependent on federal tax credits (IRA: Production Tax Credit and Investment Tax Credit). Any legislative changes or reductions in these incentives could undermine project economics.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk for U.S. portfolio (73% of total). Technical but critical language: IRA tax credits (PTC, ITC) are fundamental to valuation. Trend is new/increasing with explicit references to IRA adjustments. Regulation category heavily weighted. Legislative changes could drastically reduce returns.

risks.title: Project construction financing risk
risks.summary: The company must finance the construction of 3.9 GW of additional capacity and develop 8.1 GW in pre-construction. Equity and debt requirements are substantial and depend on access to capital markets and interest rate conditions.
risks.score_rationale: Large construction (3.9 GW) and pre-construction (8.1 GW) portfolio requires substantial financing. Language is implicit but critical: 'required equity during construction estimated at 10%'. Trend is increasing with rapid pipeline expansion. Capital category is existential for growth.

risks.title: PPA contract signing risk
risks.summary: Several major pre-construction projects do not yet have signed power purchase agreements (PPAs). The absence of PPAs delays financing and exposes the company to volatile market pricing.
risks.score_rationale: Multiple major projects without signed PPAs ('PPA to be signed'): Nardo (97 MW, 1.3 GWh), Tapolca BESS (140 MWh), Israel Storage (813 MWh), Yatir (38 MW). Neutral language but absence of contracts is a critical commercial risk. Trend is stable but structural to pipeline. Impacts bankability.

risks.title: Geographic concentration and political risks
risks.summary: The company operates in geopolitically sensitive regions (Israel, MENA, Eastern Europe). Political tensions, conflicts or instabilities could disrupt operations, delay projects or affect contracts with local authorities.
risks.score_rationale: Portfolio exposed to Israel (mature and development), MENA (Iftach), Eastern Europe (Serbia, Croatia, Hungary, Kosovo). Neutral language but tense geopolitical context (Israel-Hamas, regional tensions). Trend is increasing with MENA expansion. Geopolitical category weighted.

risks.title: Tax-equity partnership risk
risks.summary: The company finances its U.S. projects through tax-equity partners who take a share of cash flows (5-19% depending on project). Partnership terms are variable and market-dependent, creating uncertainty over net returns.
risks.score_rationale: Numerous projects with tax-equity partners (Atrisco PV/BESS: 17.5%-19% share, 5-10 year term). Technical language but structural dependency. Trend is stable but growing with U.S. pipeline. Capital category weighted. Commercial terms variable ('subject to market conditions').

risks.title: Development pipeline execution risk
risks.summary: The development portfolio (11.2 GW) represents a major expansion. Execution depends on permitting, component availability, construction capacity and supply chain stability.
risks.score_rationale: Large pipeline (19.3 GW total), with 11.2 GW in late-stage development. Neutral language but implicit execution risk. Trend is increasing with rapid expansion. Industrial category weighted. Construction timelines, permitting, and supply chains are critical.

ai_positioning.summary: AI impact mentioned as a driver of electricity demand through data center expansion, but not positioned as a core operational lever for the company.
evidence: Reference to increased adoption of machine learning and AI driving electricity demand for data centers
U.S. PPA prices rising due to broader use of electricity in information technology sectors
No mention of AI-driven optimization for project operations, energy forecasting, or internal processes
